newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on loss skepticism.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on loss skepticism.

text.p: Skepticism that a large amount of wheat was lost to a weekend freeze in the U.S. Great Plains knocked CBOT wheat futures to a lower close Wednesday, traders said.
"There's a little pressure again on the crop estimate," a trader said.

Wheat dropped Tuesday, after rallying the 20-cent limit Monday, with Tuesday's pressure coming from talk a closely followed private crop analyst estimated the weekend freeze loss in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat crop at only 50 million bushels, traders said.
There had been loss estimates from 50 million bushels up to 200 million bushels or more.
But an agronomist for a private analytical firm Tuesday said he cut his estimate for the Kansas crop by roughly 85 million bushels.

Fred Fisher, manager of Crop-timizer in Sublette, Kansas said he had revised his estimates of the Kansas crop to about 320 million bushels from his prior estimate of approximately 405 million bushels.
Wheat closed one to nine cents lower, with May down nine at $4.06-3/4 per bushel and July down 6-1/4 at $4.15-1/2.
Also Wednesday, experts said high wheat prices and limitations caused by the spring application of herbicides should limit abandonment of whet in Kansas following last wekend's freeze.

"We have a spring wheat crop that is in danger because of flooding in the northern plains, and the price of wheat is high," said Lynn Rundle, chief executive of the 21st Century Alliance, a group of 700 Kansas wheat producers.
"We won't know for awhile on damage to the wheat crop. It may be a couple of weeks before we know," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 25,000 contracts, below the 42,553 traded Tuesday.

Spread trading was active with Goldenberg Hehmeyer doing 2.5 million July/May at seven to eight cens, premium July, LIT America did 1.5 million July/May at six to eight cents and Refco Inc spread two million May/July at eight cents, premium July, traders said.
In wheat options, Paine Webber sold 200 September $5.00 calls at 10-1/2 cents and Refco Inc sold 100 July $3.80 puts at 8-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, below the 21,822 traded Tuesday.
